title: Great News! I'm Raising A PE Fund!
subtitle: Sort of a joke but I'll do it if you want to be an LP
text:
Ok. So the business model for PE (private equity) in healthcare is good for PE. The standard is 2% Management Fees and 20% on profits.

I have discussed how bad this is for healthcare. And how bad it is for Limited Partners (a.k.a. investors).

Well, if anyone wants to make me a fund manager, I have an investment fund hypothesis you will like:

We are called DoubleDown Health Partners. We are Doubling down on our value based care investment thesis. I have no idea if it will work. However, I can promise you will love our fee structure.

We charge 1% annual fees. That is Half the competition. We also only take 10% on profits.

That is it. That is the whole business.

I’ll invest in responsible health things only. I won’t promise the moon. But I’ll take less of your money.

DoubleDown Health Partners. Who’s an LP?

I’ll leave comments open on this one. Accredited investors only.

—Owen Muir, M.D.

Managing Director,

DoubleDown Health Partners.
